clue.text: Whom Mark C replaced and aimed to unmask at the eleventh hour

parts.note: Mark Carney replaced Justin Trudeau as Canadian PM; written the same way, forename plus initial, he is Justin T

indicators.note: a mask covers the face's edges; taking it off strips AIMED of its outer letters

parts.note: the inside of aIMEd

explanation.surface: A detective story in which someone called Mark C takes over a case and plans to expose the villain at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark C looks like a character in a thriller; he is Mark Carney, Canada's Prime Minister, and the clue's own style of forename plus initial tells you to write his predecessor as Justin T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the eleventh hour is done just in time, at the last possible moment.

clue.text: Dieter's agreed with working out prank

parts.note: ja is German for yes, what a German called Dieter says when he agrees
PE = physical education, working out

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet agrees to exercise as a bit of a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Dieter is not someone on a diet but a German man's name, so his agreement is JA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jape is an old-fashioned word for a practical joke, so it is a plain synonym for prank.

clue.text: Corporation provides support for music etc from the ground level

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that supports another sits underneath it
read from the bottom of a down entry upwards

parts.note: music is one of the arts
a corporation is jokey old slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A big company announces it will fund music and the arts at grassroots level.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation reads as a business sponsor; it is the old joke word for a pot belly, TUM. The words 'ground level' run together in the surface, but 'level' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or level, of rock or of society.

clue.text: Futile news I'm surprised to receive when the chips are down

parts.note: inane = pointless, futile
'Mercy!' is an exclamation of surprise
gen = information, the news

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to be told something pointless at a moment of crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is hearing 'I'm surprised' as the exclamation MERCY rather than a statement; GEN is the British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: When the chips are down means when things get serious, which is what in an emergency means.

clue.text: Zealots waving "bye" on board, heading for hell

indicators.note: the letters of ZEALOTS move about like a waved flag

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

indicators.note: the head, first letter, of Bye

parts.note: the first letter of Bye

explanation.surface: Fanatics on a ship's deck wave goodbye as they sail off to damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for hell' does double duty: 'heading' takes the first letter of bye, and 'hell' closes the definition, since 'go to blazes' means go to hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To blazes is a euphemism for to hell, as in 'go to blazes'.

clue.text: London coppers taking against Houses of Parliament painter

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
on = against, as in leaning on the wall

explanation.surface: The London police take against a painter at work outside Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking against' reads as disliking; it splits into the container instruction and ON. Monet painted a famous series of the Houses of Parliament in fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet painted the Houses of Parliament many times from across the Thames.

clue.text: Black suits winning swimmer

parts.note: spades and clubs are the two black suits in cards
up = ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A card player holding the black suits is ahead of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is the crossword's way of saying fish; the scup is a porgy caught off the American Atlantic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The scup is a fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: French patriot announced vehicle for exhibition

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken, so the letters come from sound

parts.note: a show van displays goods, and said aloud it matches the French name

explanation.surface: A French patriot is paraded in a display vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Chauvin was the legendary fanatical soldier of Napoleon who gave us the word chauvinism.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauvin was a (possibly mythical) French soldier famed for his extreme patriotism.

clue.text: Foremost of foodies with baked topless tarts in mind for son?

definitions.text: Foremost of foodies with baked topless tarts in mind for son?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within what is left of the mind word
for means in place of, so the son letter leaves to make way for the tarts

parts.note: the psyche is the mind or soul
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: baked means cooked and so transformed, signalling a rearrangement of the letters
topless means without the top, the first letter of the word

parts.note: its letters, minus the top one, are the fodder

indicators.note: foremost means the front, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook with a foodie following thinks about baking open tarts for a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the T off TARTS, and 'baked' turns ARTS into ASTR. That goes 'in' PSYCHE 'for' (in place of) its S, giving PASTRYCHE, then the F of foodies ends it. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry chef is a cook who specialises in baked goods such as tarts, so the whole clue paints one at work.

clue.text: My parents have run through Italian city

parts.note: pa and ma, both parents
R = run, as on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: Someone's parents have dashed through an Italian city on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is R, the cricket abbreviation, split between the two parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Not many bones broken

indicators.note: the letters of MANY BONES are broken apart and reset

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: An X-ray shows only a few fractures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not many' looks like one phrase, but 'Not' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: By no means is an emphatic 'not', as in 'by no means certain'.

clue.text: New Romantic style, for sure

indicators.note: the letters are made new, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: The New Romantic look of the 1980s, without a doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: New Romantic reads as the 1980s pop movement, which hides 'New' as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Most certainly and for sure both express firm agreement.

clue.text: Pay host, revert to work!

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: Orders at the end of a night out: settle with the host and get back to your job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the fodder and what you say when the fun is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying the host and heading back to work is exactly what the party's over means.

clue.text: Facility for genetic engineering support line on which one catches up

indicators.note: in a down clue, the phrase reads upwards
the reversed piece sits on top of the rest in a down entry

parts.note: I (one) + LAND, catch, as with a fish
a bra is a support garment
RY = railway line

explanation.surface: A laboratory describes a support line that someone grabs onto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches up' looks like a phrase meaning draws level; split it and 'catches' is LAND, 'up' the upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A DNA library is a collection of cloned DNA fragments used in genetic engineering.

clue.text: Tranquillised, deer dizzily came to

parts.note: numb = deadened, tranquillised

indicators.note: the letters of DEER spin round

parts.note: rearranged to ERED

explanation.surface: A deer shot with a tranquilliser dart comes round, still woozy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' reads as regaining consciousness; it is the definition in the sense of amounting to a total.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd that numbered thousands came to thousands.

clue.text: One section of cultural significance

parts.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
a conic is a conic section, the curve made by slicing a cone

explanation.surface: One part of something is held to matter culturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' is the geometry sense: a conic section, called a conic for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is widely recognised as culturally significant.

clue.text: Overnight they provided the necessary recommended volume

definitions.meaning: 'the necessary' is a euphemism for relieving oneself; these pots were kept under the bed for the night
the dictionary British setters and solvers treat as the standard reference

explanation.surface: A hotel supplied everything required overnight, including the suggested reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamber pots served the night's needs, and Chambers is also a big British dictionary, the crossword solver's usual reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamber pots served the night-time necessities, and Chambers is the dictionary solvers are pointed to.

clue.text: Releases Come With Me

definitions.meaning: to release is to stop holding on to something
the invitation you give when you want company as you leave

explanation.surface: A music listing: the latest releases include a song called Come With Me.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals dress 'Come With Me' as a song title among new 'releases'; both are simply definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lets go means releases, and 'Let's go' is an invitation to come along.

clue.text: If this is set it's fairly stormy

definitions.text: If this is set it's fairly stormy

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about as in a storm

parts.note: the anagram of IF plus the answer
take IF away from ITSFAIRLY to leave the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A sailor's rule of thumb: when this sail goes up, the weather is rough.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: IF plus 'this' (the answer) rearranged gives IT'S FAIRLY. As a whole, it describes the sail too, since a trysail is set in heavy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A trysail is a small strong sail hoisted in storms in place of the mainsail.

clue.text: Swinger incensing wife visiting northern island

parts.note: Thule, the ancients' far-northern island
rib = wife, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A swinger enraging his wife by dropping in on an island in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' is not a partner-swapper but something swung, and 'incensing' means giving out incense, not angering. RIB for wife is an old joke from Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurible is a censer swung on chains to spread incense in church.

clue.text: The quickest to the buzzer?

definitions.meaning: reads as the fastest contestant; really the most direct route
reads as a quiz-show buzzer; really an insect that buzzes, whose flight home is famously straight

explanation.surface: A quiz show: who is fastest on the buzzer?
explanation.walkthrough: The buzzer is a bee, and the quickest route to it is the line it flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the most direct route, named after the bee, a buzzer.

clue.text: Unrivalled in the sack, that MC, it's rumoured

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
yon = that, in poetry and dialect

indicators.note: what is rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so sound gives the spelling

parts.note: a compère is a Master of Ceremonies

explanation.surface: Gossip that a host of ceremonies is peerless between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides three plain pieces; YON is the old word for that, and compère the British name for an MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrivalled means nothing can match it, and beyond compare is the idiom for something past all comparison.

clue.text: What makes bitch bite quarry?

parts.note: the two letters of bitch that must change to make bite
the change is made by reading one thing as another
the letter of bite that stands where the pair stood

explanation.surface: What provokes a female dog into biting her prey?
explanation.walkthrough: To turn BITCH into BITE you read CH as E, and that instruction spells the answer. The dog surface makes 'quarry' look like part of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The chase can mean the hunted animal itself, the quarry.

clue.text: A little bit hard to get into Wilde?

indicators.note: to get into a place is to go inside it

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the great wit
H = hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's work is a touch difficult to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilde stands for WIT by example, which the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'.

clue.text: Whatever happens, however quickly?

definitions.meaning: in any case, no matter what

explanation.surface: A shrug: whatever happens, and however fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: rate as speed, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: At any rate means in any case, and read literally, at whatever speed.

clue.text: Series included between six and nine nicker

indicators.note: included means contained within, so the answer is what sits inside the run, its end letter shed too
the series is the run of numbers between six and nine, and only part of that run is wanted, so its opening is dropped

parts.note: the numbers between six and nine are seven and eight, written together as SEVENEIGHT

explanation.surface: A set of things falls somewhere between six and nine, and one is a nicker.
explanation.walkthrough: The series of numbers between six and nine is seven, eight; the answer is included in 'seveN EIGHt', so SEVE and T fall away. 'nicker' is not the slang for a pound here but a noun for a thing that nickers.
explanation.definitionFit: To nicker is to whinny softly, as a horse does, so a neigh is a horse's call or nicker.

clue.text: Locksmith postpones returning, out of policeman's custody

indicators.note: what is left goes back the other way

parts.note: delays = postpones
DS = Detective Sergeant, held in custody inside DELAYS; freeing it leaves ELAY

explanation.surface: A locksmith keeps putting off coming back and escapes from police custody.
explanation.walkthrough: The custody is DELAYS holding D and S; free the DS and ELAY reads backwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Linus Yale Jr invented the pin-tumbler lock that bears his name.

clue.text: The essence of Cavern's mastery, stirringly staging live Sixties music

indicators.note: the letters are stirred into a new order
the essence is the heart, the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of CavErn's
anagram fodder with the E
to be = to live, exist

explanation.surface: A review praises the Cavern Club's stirring live show of Sixties music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cavern was the Liverpool club where the Beatles made their name, so the whole surface belongs to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Merseybeat was the 1960s Liverpool pop sound of the Beatles and their contemporaries.
